CloudFormation reports a custom resource update as a conditional replacement because the handler could answer with a new physical id. RouterConfigApplier's handler returns the physical id it was given (router-config), so a changed zip key re-applies the router config files in place and nothing is replaced or deleted (a replace would only re-run the same idempotent apply; its Delete does nothing).

The router no longer invokes the procedure runner; it puts a wake on the site's queue (PPY-567bf9). Its permission to invoke the runner is replaced by RouterWakeQueuePolicy, which may send to the wake queues and nothing else.
